_schema: PRIVATE per-peer setup (book Appendix B). Never crosses the network, never signed, never negotiated. Contains no secrets -- API keys and OAuth credentials come from environment variables only (guidelines §7.4).

opponents._remark: Terms the book leaves to inter-team agreement that are genuinely PER-PAIR rather than league-wide. They live here, in the private unsigned setup, because game.json is hashed into config_sha256 -- adding a key there would move a digest both peers have already verified. Defaults are first_half + multiplicative_book_v1, so an opponent absent from this table is played on the book's own terms.

imreeyal._remark: The copthief-league-protocol kit's published forms, which anrbj666 and uoh-sqak also play. Under odd_even the first-sorted group is cop on sub-games 1/3/5, so best2934 is cop on 1/3/5 and imreeyal on 2/4/6.

opponents._tie_rule_remark: series_add | series_replace | per_subgame. Three teams can each be conformant and each compute a different total for the same level series, so this is declared rather than derived. series_add is the league's common form (this kit, imreeyal, anrbj666 -- who declared it from their own result builder in league issue #47); per_subgame is what the unmodified reference does -- it pays a drawn ROW 2 apiece and applies nothing at series level. With k drawn rows in a level series the two differ by 2(k-1), so they agree only when exactly one row drew. Under Appendix F's permanent values no row can draw at all (a technical loss pays 0/0 and is NOT a draw), so k is 0 and the two rules disagree on every level series -- there is no case a pair could play that would reveal it first.
opponents._counted_remark: counted | counted_sign_off. A pairing is UNCOUNTED unless a human writes both here: `counted: true` plus the sign-off sentence naming where both operators agreed in writing. They feed result_*.json's `league` block -- the machine-readable marker rule 52 hangs on, which imreeyal and best2934 both lacked until league issue #45. No code path writes these two keys, and that is the point: arming the marker is a person editing a file. An armed marker with an empty sign-off disarms itself, because `counted: true` with nothing behind it is the shape a copied fixture makes and it is a false declaration under rules 37-38. Absent means friendly.

network._remark: public_url is this role's path behind the shared front door (tools/frontdoor.py). Both roles are served at once from one reserved ngrok domain, so nothing is repointed between sub-games -- required by the odd/even role convention, where the role flips at every sub-game rather than once at half time.

strategy._remark: brain accepts 'package.module:Class' so a strategy can be swapped without touching the engine (guidelines §12.1, extension points).
strategy._barrier_engage_range_remark: Tuned from 4 to 1 on measured evidence (results/sweep.json, results/robustness.json). A barrier costs a turn of movement, so engaging from a distance leaves the cop standing still while the thief walks away -- and under the agreed one-turn scent lag the belief peak it was aiming at is probably wrong too. Re-measured under that lag, the curve is a cliff rather than a slope: capture 1.000 at range 1, 0.950 at 2, then 0.000 at 3 and 0.025 at 4. Verified against five structurally different thieves, not only the one the sweep used -- range 1 has the best worst case (0.925) of every level tested. NOTE the class default in CopBrain is still 4; this file is what we field, and measuring the class defaults instead is exactly the fault recorded as ADR-025.

trash_talk._remark: provider: template | ollama | claude_api | claude_cli. 'template' costs zero tokens and is the default, because the book requires the match to be playable with no LLM at all.

email._remark: recipient is overwritten at load time with the address fixed by Appendix F Table 20 -- a team cannot opt out of reporting by redirecting it.
